description: A draft that explains each reviewed finding, its severity and the coordinator's decision as the input gives them. The reviewer should pass it.

target.executive_summary: The repository has one finding that needs prompt attention: a signing key written into settings.py [SEC-1]. A permissive cross-origin setting [CFG-1] and an open version range [HYG-1] are smaller matters, and no known-vulnerable dependency was reported. Rotating the signing key comes first.

sections.prose: A framework signing key is written into settings.py at line 4 [SEC-1]. It is rated high, because anyone who can read the repository can use it to forge signed session data. Generate a new key, read it from the environment and treat sessions signed with the old key as untrusted. The coordinator accepted this examination after the reviewer found nothing to challenge.

One medium finding concerns app.py at line 9 [CFG-1]: every response allows requests from any origin. List the origins that need access instead. The coordinator accepted this examination after the reviewer found nothing to challenge.

No known-vulnerable dependency was reported. The examiner looked up the one pinned package, flask 3.0.3, and OSV lists no advisory for it. The requests entry has no exact version, so it could not be looked up. The coordinator accepted this examination.
One medium finding concerns requirements.txt at line 2 [HYG-1]: the requests entry has an open version range. Pin an exact version and add a lockfile. The coordinator accepted this examination.

steps.rationale: The reviewer passed the examination and its finding is supported.

disposition.summary: All four steps were examined and reviewed, and no challenge is open.

EX-SEC-v1.summary: Read settings.py and app.py. One credential is written into the code.

findings.title: Signing key written into settings.py
findings.evidence: SECRET_KEY = "<redacted:k7Z…>" is a literal signing key that anyone who can read the repository can use to forge signed session data.
findings.recommendation: Generate a new key, read it from the environment and treat sessions signed with the old key as untrusted.

EX-CFG-v1.summary: Read app.py. One setting is permissive.

findings.title: Responses allow requests from any origin
findings.recommendation: List the origins that need access instead of allowing every one.

limitations: The requests entry has no exact version, so it could not be looked up.

findings.title: requests has an open version range
findings.recommendation: Pin an exact version and add a lockfile.
